Edn1 DRG snRNA-seq cell type pitfalls
pitfalls snRNA-seq marker panel annotation

label: Use per-factor R2 of PC1
text: PITFALL: Variance explained in PC1 by a categorical factor must be computed as R2 (eta-squared) from regressing PC1 scores on the one-hot factor; using Pearson correlation with integer-coded labels or the PC's own variance ratio gives meaningless rankings. CHECK: For each factor (cytokine, donor, cell_type, treatment), fit PC1 ~ C(factor) separately and record R2 = between-group SS / total SS of PC1. IF FOUND: If someone used label-encoded correlation, redo as one-way ANOVA R2 per factor. SOURCE: https://rdrr.io/bioc/scater/man/getExplanatoryPCs.html ; https://scib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/scib.metrics.pc_regression.html

label: Many-level factor R2 inflation
text: PITFALL: Plain R2 grows with the number of factor levels, so a 91-level cytokine factor (90 df) absorbs some variance by chance while a 2-level treatment factor cannot. CHECK: Compare R2 with adjusted R2 for each factor, and compare against a permutation null (shuffle labels, recompute R2) per factor. IF FOUND: If cytokine's raw R2 is close to its permutation null or its adjusted R2 drops below another factor's, rank on adjusted R2 and say that the ordering depends on the metric; with hundreds of thousands of cells the inflation is usually small, so verify rather than assume. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/variancePartition/inst/doc/rnd_effects.html ; https://janhove.github.io/posts/2016-04-22-r-squared/index.html

label: Treatment nested in cytokine
text: PITFALL: Treatment (PBS vs cytokine) is a coarsening of the cytokine factor if PBS is one level of 'cytokine', so R2(treatment) <= R2(cytokine) by construction and the two are not independent factors. CHECK: Crosstab treatment vs cytokine; confirm PBS appears as a cytokine level and each cytokine maps to one treatment value. IF FOUND: Expect treatment last relative to cytokine mathematically; do not run joint Type-I models with treatment entered after cytokine (it gets 0). Report marginal R2 for each factor. SOURCE: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/DMAR/vignettes/sums_of_squares.html

label: Marginal vs partial R2 ranking
text: PITFALL: In an unbalanced design, marginal (one factor at a time) R2, sequential Type-I R2 and partial/Type-II R2 can give different rankings when factors are correlated (e.g. cell-type composition differing by donor or cytokine). CHECK: Crosstab cell_type x donor and cell_type x cytokine proportions; compute both marginal R2 and Type-II (each factor adjusted for the others) R2 for PC1. IF FOUND: The question asks 'variance explained' per factor, so report marginal R2 as primary; if the rankings differ, flag it and give both. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.6339/jds.201407_12(3).0001 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5123296/

label: Normalize before PCA; depth drives PC1
text: PITFALL: PC1 of non-normalized or improperly transformed scRNA-seq counts often tracks sequencing depth or detection rate instead of biology, which changes which factor PC1 aligns with. CHECK: Inspect X (are values integer raw counts or already log-normalized?); after PCA, correlate PC1 with log1p_total_counts / gene_count from obs. IF FOUND: Run the standard pipeline (normalize_total to 1e4, log1p, HVG ~2000, scale with max_value=10, PCA) before regressing PC1 on factors; if |r(PC1, depth)| stays high, report it as a caveat and check whether depth differs by donor/cell type. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5

label: Check ranking robustness to preprocessing
text: PITFALL: The PC1 result depends on preprocessing choices (HVG selection, scaling, whether HVGs are chosen per batch), and a ranking that flips between reasonable pipelines is not robust. CHECK: Recompute PC1 factor R2 under at least two settings (e.g. HVG+scale vs HVG without scale, or a different subsample seed) and see whether the ordering holds. IF FOUND: If the top-ranked factor changes, report the standard scanpy pipeline result as primary and note the instability. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbagrm.2024.195058 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7324639/

label: Edn1 means on uncorrected log1p CP10K
text: PITFALL: Edn1 means get computed on the wrong matrix, such as integrated, scaled/z-scored, or batch-corrected values. Integration (RPCA) only corrects the low-dimensional embedding, and scaled data can turn the ranking of cell types upside down. CHECK: Confirm that the matrix used for Step 5 is log1p(counts / total_counts * 1e4) from raw X; the values must be >=0 and unscaled, and Edn1 must be zero in nuclei whose raw count is zero. IF FOUND: Use integration only for PCA/kNN/clustering, then recompute Edn1 means from the unintegrated log1p CP10K. SOURCE: https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/integration.html

label: Stratify subsampling of large data
text: PITFALL: The dataset is large (~1.6 GB h5ad), and naive random subsampling can drop rare cytokine x donor x cell-type combinations or distort the design, which biases per-factor R2. CHECK: If subsampling, compare factor level counts before and after; use backed mode or stratified sampling by sample/cytokine. IF FOUND: Use a stratified subsample (equal cells per sample or per cytokine x donor) or the full data with sparse PCA (arpack). SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/preprocessing.html

label: Verify X is raw counts
text: PITFALL: The dataset (159007346.node) has no counts layer, and X might not be raw even though the task says to use X. CHECK: Before any processing, verify that X holds non-negative integers and that its row sums match obs total_counts; obs n_genes_raw should equal the count>0 per row. IF FOUND: If X is already log-normalized, back-transform it or flag it; never normalize twice. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.basic/normalization.html

label: Use PC1 loadings to sanity-check
text: PITFALL: Donor effects in PBMC data can be driven by a few sex-linked or genotype genes (XIST, RPS4Y1, HLA) and by donor-level cell composition, and these can load onto top PCs. CHECK: Look at PC1's top-loading genes: are they cell-type markers (e.g. CD3E, CD14, MS4A1, NKG7), interferon/cytokine-response genes, or sex/HLA genes? IF FOUND: Use the loadings to sanity-check the R2 ranking (marker genes mean cell type, ISGs mean cytokine, sex/HLA genes mean donor); if they disagree with the R2, recheck the preprocessing. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10872590/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11912664/

label: Ambient RNA blurs per-type means
text: PITFALL: In snRNA-seq, ambient (soup) RNA from abundant or high-expressing cells leaks into every nucleus. Cluster means of a gene can then show up in cell types that do not express it, which flattens the ranking between cell types. CHECK: Compare Edn1 detection fraction (percent of nuclei with count>0) with the mean for each major type. A real source shows a high detection fraction in one type; ambient signal looks like a low, uniform fraction across all types. IF FOUND: Report detection fraction alongside the means. Do not decontaminate (the task fixes the method), but check whether the top two types are close enough that ambient noise could swap them. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.03.09.483658

label: Mixed/doublet clusters mislabeled
text: PITFALL: Clusters can contain doublets or mixtures, for example neuron+SGC (they are physically attached in DRG) or endothelial+mural (tightly associated pericytes). Such a cluster carries two marker sets and gets mislabeled, which can move Edn1 signal to the wrong major type. CHECK: For each cluster, print the mean and percent-expressing of every marker panel (Isl1/Prph, Fabp7/Kcnj10, Pecam1/Flt1, Rgs5/Notch3, Col1a1/Pdgfra, C1qa/Aif1, etc.). Flag clusters where two panels are both high, and look at where the Edn1-high cluster sits. IF FOUND: Label by the dominant panel using a z-scored panel score per cluster. Make sure the Edn1-high cluster's label is unambiguous, and test whether the answer depends on how the mixed cluster is labeled. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7703774/

label: Endothelial vs mural separation
text: PITFALL: Endothelial and mural cells are closely related in DRG, and Rgs5, Notch3 and Flt1 can be shared between pericytes and endothelium at low levels. At resolution 0.6 the two can merge into one vascular cluster, and how that cluster is labeled decides the answer between the vascular options. CHECK: Check whether Pecam1/Flt1-high and Rgs5/Notch3-high nuclei fall in separate clusters. Within the Edn1-high cluster, compute Edn1 in Pecam1+ versus Rgs5+ nuclei. Use extra markers to confirm (endothelial: Cldn5, Ly6c1; mural: Vtn, Kcnj8, Acta2). IF FOUND: If vascular cells are merged, subcluster them or assign labels per cell by marker panel score, and report Edn1 for each subtype separately. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(22)00044-4

label: n_genes filter depletes small nuclei
text: PITFALL: A fixed n_genes>1000 filter is a nucleus-type-dependent cut. It removes many small, low-RNA non-neuronal nuclei (immune, vascular, some glia) and keeps neurons, so some major types may end up with very few nuclei and noisy means. CHECK: After filtering, report the number of nuclei per major type and per sample. Flag any type with fewer than about 50 nuclei, or one present in only one sample. IF FOUND: Keep the filter, since the task requires it, but report the per-type n and a bootstrap CI or per-sample means for the top types. If the winner is a tiny group, say so. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9912498/

label: Leiden seed/implementation instability
text: PITFALL: Leiden/Louvain results depend on implementation (leidenalg vs igraph flavor, directed vs undirected graph, Seurat SNN vs scanpy UMAP-weighted kNN) and on seed, so 'seed=0' does not make results identical across tools. Cluster boundaries for small populations may change. CHECK: Rerun clustering with 2-3 other seeds or flavors and check whether the major-type label of the Edn1-high cluster and the top-ranked type stay the same (ARI between runs, top type each time). IF FOUND: If the top type changes between runs, assign labels per nucleus from marker scores instead of per cluster, or report the instability. SOURCE: https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/1531

label: RPCA implementation and overcorrection
text: PITFALL: Scanpy has no built-in RPCA. If an analyst swaps in harmony or BBKNN without saying so, or over-integrates (with only 3 samples, the two age groups are confounded with sample), rare types such as mural or immune can be absorbed into neighboring clusters. CHECK: Batch = obs 'sample' (3 levels: e.g. 3M, ...). Compare clusters with and without integration; confirm each major type still forms its own cluster and is present in every sample. IF FOUND: Use a real RPCA implementation (Seurat IntegrateLayers RPCAIntegration, or the Python ports omicverse methods='rpca' / trackcell) or say clearly which substitute was used. If rare types merge after integration, lower the integration strength (k.anchor) or label from marker scores per cell. SOURCE: https://satijalab.org/seurat/archive/v4.3/integration_rpca

label: Label-to-option mapping
text: PITFALL: The internal major labels must map onto the answer options, and some labels (Schwann, T_cell, B_cell) are not options. A mapping mistake, such as calling the Neuron label something other than 'Sensory neurons' or treating SGC as Schwann, changes the letter. CHECK: Rank all labeled major types by mean Edn1, including non-option types. If a non-option type (e.g. Schwann) comes out on top, record that, then choose the highest among the option types. Make sure every option type actually received at least one cluster. IF FOUND: Report the full ranking and the mapping Endothelial->A, Fibroblast->B, Mural->C, SGC->D, Neuron->E, Macrophage->F explicitly. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.basic/cell-type-annotation.html

label: Mean log1p CP10K interpretation
text: PITFALL: The mean of log1p CP10K mixes two things, detection rate and expression level. Total-count normalization also removes real differences in RNA content between large neurons and small non-neuronal nuclei, so a type with a few very high nuclei can beat one with broad moderate expression. CHECK: For the top 2-3 types, report the mean, the fraction of nuclei expressing, and the mean among expressing nuclei, plus per-sample means. IF FOUND: The task defines the metric as the mean of log1p CP10K over all nuclei, so use it. If the top two are within noise or the order changes between samples, report that instability. SOURCE: https://multiomeacademy.com/tutorials/scrna-seq/session_04_normalization_hvg_pca.html

label: Panel mean dominated by high-expression genes
text: PITFALL: An unscaled mean of log-normalized expression over a 4-5 gene panel is dominated by whichever genes are highly or broadly expressed (e.g. Apoe, Glul, Mbp, Tubb3, Col1a2), so argmax assignment reflects panel composition rather than identity; one strongly specific gene (e.g. Rgs5) can be outvoted by three near-zero panel-mates. CHECK: print the full cluster x gene mean table (not just panel averages); for each cluster list the top-scoring and runner-up lineage with the margin; look for clusters where a single panel gene is top-ranked across clusters but its lineage loses the argmax; re-run assignment after z-scoring each gene across clusters (or using fraction-expressing) and see if labels change. IF FOUND: report the task-specified unscaled result as asked, but in the interpretation attribute the outcome to the averaging method, and note which cluster the specific marker points to. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/3845 ; https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.09.20.558114

label: Nuclear detection bias of marker genes
text: PITFALL: snRNA-seq captures nuclear RNA; genes whose transcripts are short, rapidly exported or mainly cytoplasmic (often cytoskeletal/contractile genes like Acta2, also some secreted/structural genes) are detected at much lower levels in nuclei than in whole cells, while long intron-rich genes are favoured. A panel containing such genes is deflated. CHECK: for every panel gene, compute fraction of nuclei with >0 counts and max cluster mean; flag genes that are near-zero in every cluster (these drag their panel average down uniformly). Compare mural genes Rgs5, Notch3, Pdgfrb, Acta2 individually. IF FOUND: treat that lineage's panel score as biased low; state in the interpretation that the nuclear detection asymmetry, not biology, drives the result. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10984380/ ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/bioinformatics/articles/10.3389/fbinf.2023.1144266/full ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5519641/

label: Mural vs fibroblast overlap
text: PITFALL: Pdgfrb and Acta2 (and Cspg4) are broadly expressed across mesenchymal cells including fibroblasts, so mural and fibroblast panels overlap; mural cells may be absorbed into fibroblast clusters, or conversely the overlap may be blamed when the real cause is elsewhere. CHECK: in the cluster(s) where Rgs5/Notch3 are highest, check whether fibroblast genes (Col1a1, Col1a2, Dcn, Pdgfra) are also high or low, and inspect discriminating pericyte/SMC genes Kcnj8, Vtn, Higd1b, Abcc9, Ndufa4l2, Myh11, Cspg4. If the Rgs5-high cluster is NOT fibroblast-assigned (e.g. it went to endothelial or another lineage) or has low Col1a1/Dcn, fibroblast absorption is not the explanation. IF FOUND: only choose the fibroblast-absorption interpretation if the mural-marker-high nuclei sit inside a fibroblast-assigned cluster with high fibroblast panel genes. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17740-1 ; https://www.cell.com/trends/cell-biology/fulltext/S0962-8924(23)00111-3

label: Ambient RNA inflates broad panels
text: PITFALL: Ambient (cell-free) RNA in droplet snRNA-seq, predominantly neuronal and glial in nervous tissue, adds a baseline of abundant transcripts (e.g. Apoe, Mbp, Snap25, Tubb3) to every nucleus, inflating panels built from those genes in all clusters and shifting argmax away from small lineages. CHECK: look at mean expression of neuronal/glial panel genes in clearly non-neuronal clusters (macrophage, endothelial); if consistently nonzero across all clusters, ambient contamination is present. IF FOUND: note that panels containing ambient-prone genes get a uniform boost; consider comparing using fraction-expressing or relative (z-scored) scores as a sensitivity check; optionally SoupX/CellBender if raw droplets were available. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7763177/ ; https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.03.09.483658

label: Score on full log-normalized matrix
text: PITFALL: Subsetting the AnnData to the 3,000 HVGs (adata = adata[:, hvg]) or scoring on scaled data drops or distorts marker genes; panel means then come from a subset of genes or from z-scaled values with negative means. CHECK: confirm every panel gene is present in var_names of the matrix you score on (watch symbol mismatches, e.g. Ncmap) and that scores come from the full log1p-normalized matrix (adata.raw or a saved layer), not adata.X after scale/HVG subset. IF FOUND: recompute panel means on full log-normalized data, averaging only genes present, and report missing genes. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pl.dotplot.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2909

label: Leiden seed and implementation sensitivity
text: PITFALL: Leiden results depend on the neighbor graph, random seed and the implementation (leidenalg vs igraph flavor); cluster counts and boundaries of small populations can change, which changes nuclei totals per lineage. CHECK: use scanpy defaults for neighbors (n_neighbors=15, default n_pcs) and record scanpy version, flavor and random_state=0; re-run with 2-3 seeds and see if the lineage nuclei count is stable. IF FOUND: report the default-seed result and note instability; do not change resolution to get a different answer (resolution is fixed by the task). SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7852188/ ; https://casrai.org/guides/leiden-clustering-single-cell

label: Verify mural cells exist before blaming biology
text: PITFALL: Before blaming rarity or dissociation loss for a missing lineage, verify whether the lineage's marker-expressing nuclei actually exist in the data; DRG snRNA atlases routinely recover vascular SMC/pericytes and mesenchymal cells, and snRNA-seq generally reduces (not increases) dissociation bias against mesenchymal/perivascular cells. CHECK: count nuclei with high Rgs5 (and Notch3/Kcnj8/Higd1b) and see whether they form a coherent cluster; check that cluster's size. IF FOUND (a coherent mural-marker-high cluster of reasonable size exists): rule out 'rare/below detection', 'nuclear isolation depletes pericytes' and 'need higher resolution' interpretations; the failure is in the annotation method. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7790136/ ; https://doi.org/10.1111/jnc.70180

label: Residual doublets in first-pass PIP-seq
text: PITFALL: 'First-pass filtered' PIP-seq data may still contain doublets and low-quality/empty barcodes; heterotypic doublet clusters show mixed panels and can win an argmax spuriously. CHECK: inspect per-cluster median total counts/genes and co-expression of mutually exclusive panels (e.g. neuron + macrophage); optionally run scrublet. IF FOUND: flag such clusters in the interpretation but keep the task-specified workflow for the reported count. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-023-01685-z ; https://www.fluentbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/PIPseeker-v3.3-User-Guide.pdf

text: FINDING: Cell-level R2 is the standard for PC variance explained in single-cell QC: scater getExplanatoryPCs/getVarianceExplained regress each PC (or gene) on each colData variable separately across all columns (cells) and report percent R2 (marginal, one variable at a time); pseudobulk is used by dreamlet (aggregateToPseudoBulk then variancePartition on sample x cell-type profiles, which removes cell type as a within-assay factor), while variancePartition itself fits a linear mixed model on whatever columns it is given (designed for bulk samples). QUESTION: Is PC variance explained by metadata computed on cells or pseudobulk, and which tools do which? In that setup cell type is not a factor within an assay, so a pseudobulk reading cannot rank cell type against donor in the same way. The cell-level eta^2 the teams used is the standard quantity for this question. HOW SURE: medium. QUESTION: In split-pool combinatorial barcoding single-cell protocols, what does the first-round barcode well encode (sample identity or something else), and is it a recognized source of technical batch effects? ANSWER: The round-1 well barcode is added by in-cell reverse transcription and is the sample-specific barcode (Parse: 'the first sample-specific barcodes are added by in-cell reverse transcription'), so it encodes sample/condition identity. In Parse/SPLiT-seq v2 each well also holds paired oligo-dT and random-hexamer barcodes, which are collapsed to the same cell. Because the well is nested within sample (donor x condition), it is confounded with donor and perturbation by design and cannot be separated from them as an independent covariate. The pages I read mention sample-quality bias in split barcoding, but none of them describes round-1 wells as a recognized independent technical batch effect. The web did not settle the batch-effect part. HOW SURE: high on what the well encodes; low on batch effects. SOURCES: https://resources.parsebiosciences.com/hubfs/Marketing%20Assets%20(External%20Files)/Technical%20Brochures/Evercode%20WT%20Tech%20Brochure%20v4.pdf, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11010347/, https://combine-lab.github.io/alevin-fry-tutorials/2022/split-seq/, https://biosails.github.io/pheniqs/splitseq_vignette.

QUESTION: How does scaling versus not scaling log-normalized HVG data usually affect whether small populations (around 0.5% of cells) separate in Leiden clustering? ANSWER: Not settled by the pages I could read. The sources say there is no consensus on scaling. Scaling weights all genes equally; without it, PCA is driven by each gene's variance and so by its mean expression. Seurat tutorials scale, while sc-best-practices and the current scanpy tutorial do not. My inference, which no source states directly: scaling boosts sparse, low-mean markers specific to a rare population, which can help it separate but also amplifies noise; without scaling, PCs are dominated by high-variance genes of large populations. Either way, a ~0.5% cluster can be seed-sensitive. The teams should test both settings with several seeds in the data instead of assuming a direction. A Nature Methods 2023 transformation benchmark (PMC10172138) reportedly found no improvement in k-NN recovery from z-scoring after shifted-log, but I saw that only in a search snippet; the full text did not load, so I did not rely on it. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2164, https://github.com/theislab/single-cell-best-practices/issues/185, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NBISweden/workshop-scRNAseq/master/compiled/labs/seurat/seurat_02_dimred.qmd.
